goal: Teach the governed review runner to read the codex wrapper's published report and record its two-line verdict section as this runner's own terminal verdict line, so a working reviewer stops being a structurally dead slot - without relaxing the single-terminal-verdict rule, the extra-decision-word refusal, or the auto-void path.
dispatcher: repo session, owner request 2026-09-08 (five oldest non-orchestrator issues)
prohibited_actions: Do not take the head SHA from reviewer text or from the report; it comes only from the runner's pinned options.headSha.
Do not relax the single-terminal-verdict rule, the extra-decision-word refusal, or the auto-void path.
Do not delete, exclude or retire the codex reviewer as a substitute for the repair.
Do not read a report for a wrapper run that did not exit 0; a stale report must never rescue a failed run.
Do not read a path outside the wrapper's own .ai/reviews/codex-<mode>-<runid>.md shape.
assumptions: ai-codex-review prints the absolute path of its published report as the final line of standard output, and writes that report to .ai/reviews/codex-<mode>-<runid>.md.
The published report carries a header table row `| reviewed commit | `<sha>` |` and one `## Result` heading written by the wrapper before the provider text.
The wrapper already guarantees exactly one `## Verdict` heading, because it counts them in the provider output before publishing.
The report's 64-character source digest must not reach the posted comment, because its first 40 hex characters read as a foreign commit sha to unambiguouslyTiedToHead.
stop_conditions: Stop if the transcription could take the head from anywhere but the runner's pinned value.
Stop if a transcribed body could be posted without passing extraVerdictLines.
Stop if the repair cannot be proven against a known-dirty report.
